What I did
- Retrieved your transactions and ran the dispute eligibility check for the charge.

What I found (first, as requested)
- Transaction ID: TX-0401
- Amount: 240.00 EUR
- Reason code: goods_not_received

Additional useful facts
- Transaction date: 2026-07-20
- Filing window: 90 days — deadline to file: 2026-10-18
- Current eligibility: eligible (checks passed)

Recommended next steps (do not open a dispute yet)
1. Contact the merchant first
   - Request shipment status or a refund and keep all replies (email, chat transcripts, support ticket IDs).
2. Gather supporting evidence
   - Order confirmation, payment receipt, shipping/tracking information, screenshots of the merchant page, timestamps of delivery attempts, and any correspondence showing the goods were not delivered.
   - Verta may request evidence; if asked, you must supply it within 7 calendar days or the case can be declined.
3. If the merchant won’t resolve it
   - Tell me to “open the dispute.” I will re-run the eligibility check (required) and, if still eligible, open the dispute on your behalf.
   
What happens next
- I will not open a dispute now. Tell me when you’ve gathered the evidence or if you want me to open the dispute and I will proceed.

fragments.text:
Dispute handling process
## Evidence requirements
The customer may be asked for supporting evidence: an order confirmation, a
delivery record, correspondence with the merchant. Failure to supply requested
evidence within 7 calendar days results in the case being declined.

Customer security policy
## Phishing
Verta communicates only through the app, the registered email address and the
in-app chat. Customers reporting a suspicious message are advised not to click
links and to forward the message to the security team.

Payment dispute rules
## Escalation on blocked disputes
When a dispute is blocked by a customer-level restriction, the case must be
escalated to a human agent.

Complaints
## Escalation to the regulator
If a customer is not satisfied with the final response they may refer the
complaint to the national financial ombudsman within six months.
